typeHints.manual: Starts when someone triggers the run manually.
typeHints.schedule: Starts at scheduled times once the workflow is turned on.
typeHints.event: Starts when something changes in the workspace or under a page.
typeHints.agent: Hands a goal to the assistant as a work item and waits for the result.
typeHints.condition: Continues along the yes or no path depending on a result field or an input.
typeHints.parallel: Starts multiple paths at the same time.
typeHints.join: Waits for multiple paths and then continues together.
typeHints.approval: Asks a person and waits for their decision.
typeHints.end: Finishes the run with an outcome.

problems.schema_invalid: This part does not have the shape expected by a workflow.
problems.no_trigger: The workflow has no trigger. Without one, it will never start.
problems.duplicate_node_id: Two nodes have the same ID.
problems.duplicate_edge_id: Two edges have the same ID.
problems.duplicate_edge: This edge exists more than once.
problems.edge_unknown_node: The edge leads to a node that does not exist.
problems.edge_invalid_handle: The edge starts from an output that this node does not have.
problems.edge_into_trigger: An edge cannot lead into a trigger.
problems.edge_self_loop: A node cannot loop back into itself.
problems.handle_multiple_targets: Multiple edges leave from this output. To branch into multiple paths, use a branch.
problems.node_multiple_inputs: Multiple edges lead into this node. To combine multiple paths, use a join.
problems.node_unreachable: No trigger leads to this node; it would never run.
problems.cycle: The edges form a loop. A workflow only runs forward.
problems.join_too_few_inputs: A join needs at least two incoming paths.
problems.join_impossible: This join waits for all paths, but two of them are mutually exclusive. It would never proceed: use “one is enough” here.
problems.parallel_too_few_branches: A branch needs at least two branches.
problems.parallel_too_many_branches: This branch has more branches than a run is allowed to have at the same time.
problems.field_required: Information is missing here that is required before publishing the workflow.
problems.output_field_invalid: An output field is invalid: a name is duplicated, or a selection is missing its values.
problems.condition_unknown_source: The condition reads from something that does not exist.
problems.condition_not_upstream: The condition reads from a node that does not run before it.
problems.condition_unknown_field: The condition reads a field that this node does not provide.
problems.condition_operator_mismatch: This comparison does not match the field type.
problems.condition_value_invalid: The comparison value is missing or does not match the field.
problems.goal_placeholder_invalid: A placeholder in the goal refers to nothing that provides an output before this node.
problems.schedule_invalid: The schedule is invalid. Check the time, time zone, and cron expression.
problems.reference_not_found: A reference points to nothing: the profile, page, or person does not exist in this workspace.

agent.goalHint: What the work item should achieve, in your own words. Insert outputs from earlier nodes and run inputs using placeholders, such as {examples}.
agent.goalPlaceholder: Look at my open technical ideas and suggest the five best next tasks.
agent.pagesHint: These pages are provided to the work item. A run triggered by a page edit prepends the modified page.
agent.writeModeHint: How freely the assistant may edit pages. The strictest mode across node, profile, and workspace always applies.
agent.budgetHint: The maximum cost for this work item, including subtasks. Empty means: the run’s budget.

completionHint.review: The workflow continues as soon as the assistant hands off the work item, unless a suggestion is still awaiting a decision.
completionHint.done: The workflow waits until a person marks the work item as done.

agent.effectiveWriteModeNarrowed: Stricter than set on the node because the profile or workspace requires it.
agent.effectiveBudgetNarrowed: Lower than set on the node because the run or profile allows less.
agent.fieldsHint: What the work item must return in structured form. Conditions and later targets read these fields, never the plain text.

event.scopeHint: Without a page, any change across the entire workspace applies.

condition.sourceHint: An output field from a node running before this condition, or an input of the run.
condition.sourceNone: No node before this condition provides output fields yet. Add fields to an agent before it, or read an input of the run.
condition.inputKeyHint: A page change provides documentId and trigger, a schedule provides scheduledFor; a manual run provides whatever is passed at start.
condition.valueInputHint: An input does not have a fixed type. Comparing against the wrong type results in “no”.

policyHint.all: Waits for every incoming path. If one is never reached, it still continues once the rest arrive.
policyHint.any: Continues with the first incoming path and never again after that. An error on another path will not fail the run.

approval.title: Title
approval.question: Question
approval.questionHint: Shown under “Waiting for you”. A condition downstream can read the answer.
approval.assigneeHint: Only a human can respond to an approval, never an agent.
approval.anybody: Anyone who can manage the workspace
approval.assigneeGone: Person is no longer a member

outcomeHint.succeeded: The run ends successfully here, and anything else still running is cancelled.
outcomeHint.failed: The run ends here as failed.
outcomeHint.cancelled: The run ends here as cancelled.

inspector.label: Name in graph
inspector.manualExplanation: A manual run starts here. Anything provided at the start can be read as input by conditions and targets.
inspector.parallelExplanation: Each branch starts at the same time. The limits of the workflow and workspace restrict how many paths a run may follow at once.
